items.difficulty_reason: After giving the old adapted-cover fiber product, degree and ramification control, the remaining author argument must show extension for reflexive symmetric differentials rather than for a metric, produce the special Aut(D)^n-invariant tensor from a canonical-power section, and convert nonzero restriction to the subvariety into a geometric alternative involving the coordinate foliations. The new proof therefore connects the order of the poles, the choice of n in the twist, and exclusion of the tangency locus. It does not re-use the ball quotient negative bisectional curvature closing as a proof of this case.

statement_spans.label: Physical p15 layout text lines 24–37. Exact Theorem 4.4 from 'Let Γ ⊂ Aut(D)^n be a discrete irreducible subgroup' through its last bigness sentence. §4.2 at lines 5–12 defines irreducibility and the foliations.

proof_spans.label: Proposition 2.19 statement at p8 line55 and its whole proof on p9 before 'We conclude this section'. Reflexive pushforward and Campana symmetric-form extension, diagram and ramification coefficient comparison. This is needed authored support, not a new ID.

§4.1 Theorem 4.1 and complete proof, physical p14 layout lines39–61, before Example 4.2. The global Γ-invariant canonical-power section is used in S^{mn} Ω, extended and twisted to compensate n(Δtilde+Dtilde) and obtain an ample-vanishing symmetric form.

Exact Theorem 4.4 proof at physical p15 layout lines39–45, through the QED before 'Finally, we observe'. It identifies the extra possible zero restriction as tangency to a coordinate foliation and excludes it by 4.3.1.

context_spans.label: Original §1 setup: neat arithmetic compactification and resolution notation, Dtilde, Δtilde, E, augmented base locus and the introduction's resolution convention. §4.4 counted only in its explicit scope; A/B and the intro C are not primary spans.

§§2.1–2.2 needed Campana orbifold/adapted-cover and symmetric cotangent definitions, reflexive powers, §2.2 local quotient setup and Proposition 2.18's fiber-product diagram/degree bound used by 2.19. Reused setup and bound are not recounted as new proof burden.
§3.1 fixed toroidal compactification/log canonical identification and opening Lemma 3.1 only as boundary context; the old Bergman curvature argument is excluded from this claim.
Physical p14 layout lines25–35. Original polydisc quotient, resolution, local stabilizer orders and boundary/exceptional divisors.

Physical p15 layout lines5–21. Irreducibility and coordinate foliations, Proposition 4.3(4.3.1) explicitly attributed to [RT18], a previously established result used in 4.4. (4.3.2) is carried on the source page but belongs to the parallel entire-curve route.
Original bibliography entry [RT18], Rousseau–Touzet, Curves in Hilbert modular varieties. The reference and its authors are distinct from the proof authors.
